missing_areas: Experimental design/data analysis (e.g., interpreting graphs or data from machine experiments)
Non-ideal machine scenarios beyond friction (e.g., deformation, slippage, real-world failure modes)
Compound machine analysis (multi-step, multi-machine systems with more than one simple machine type)
Historical context or applications of machines
Advanced conceptual reasoning (e.g., why certain machines are chosen for specific tasks, trade-offs)
issues: Many items (e.g., 001 and 003) test the same lever IMA skill with only different numbers/objects.
Items 021 and 024 are near-duplicates, both asking about angle of sliding with mass change.
Several items (e.g., 002, 005, 008, 015) are generic mechanics questions with little or no Machines-specific content.
Difficulty labeling is inconsistent: many 'difficulty 1' items are nearly identical in skill and require only formula plugging.
Too many items focus on direct calculation of IMA/AMA/efficiency with no conceptual or experimental context.
Gears are overrepresented in higher-difficulty MC items (022, 023, 030), but all test the same basic gear ratio skill.
No items require students to interpret or analyze data from an experiment or real-world scenario.
No items require students to design, critique, or improve a machine setup.
Some distractors are trivial or implausible (e.g., 004, 005, 007).
No coverage of safety, failure, or practical limitations of machines.
No items on compound machines that combine different types (e.g., lever + pulley + inclined plane).
No items on historical or real-world applications of machines.
No items on interpreting diagrams or schematics, which is common in competition.
